chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) about a man who sets out on a journey, and it is [a distance of] one day's travel.
He said: Shortening [of prayer] (qasr) is obligatory upon him if it is a journey of one day, even if he travels around for his work.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: qasr — the obligatory shortening of four-unit prayers (Zuhr, Asr, Isha) to two units during travel
key_terms.مَسِيرَةُ يَوْمٍ: a day's journey — the minimum travel threshold triggering qasr obligation in this narration
key_terms.يَدُورُ فِي عَمَلِهِ: traveling around for his work — circular or occupational travel, still qualifying for qasr

ai.seo_question: Is qasr (shortening of prayer) obligatory for a one-day journey even if the traveler circulates within his work area?
ai.summary: Ali ibn Yaqtin, a distinguished companion of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), asks about the minimum travel distance that triggers the obligation to perform qasr (shortened) prayer. The Imam rules that a single day's journey suffices to make qasr obligatory — and critically extends this ruling to encompass circular or occupational travel, closing a potential loophole for workers who do not travel in a single linear direction.
word_analysis: goes out/sets out on a journey
